## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible walk1 (branchless blend, per-particle hash RNG) with a simple walk2 render can approach the streaming ceiling on this workload.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈963 lies below all measured points, so the in-L1 regime is never observed. The L2 spill at N≈61680 falls between N=16000 and N=65000. At q=0.01, cost stays FLAT at ~62 ns/p for N=4000–16000, then dips to 57.5 at N=65000 — no rise at the L2→DRAM transition. At q=0.25, however, cost RISES from 40.3 (N=16000) to 58.4 (N=65000), marking a visible knee at the L2 spill. Beyond that, cost FALLS again at N=262000 (40.4) and continues declining to 36.5 at N=4000000, suggesting DRAM streaming amortizes per-particle overhead at large N. Death rate does not uniformly raise the floor: at N=4000000, higher churn actually lowers ns/p (48.2 at q=0.01 vs 36.5 at q=0.25), likely because dead particles skip the expensive render scatter. The N=4000 point at q=0.25 (26.9 ns/p) is anomalously low and may reflect measurement noise or a fast-path exit.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 2.53 GB/s at N=4000, q=0.25 — only 10% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling — but this point is anomalous. At stable large-N regimes, the best is 1.87 GB/s (N=4000000, q=0.25) = 7.4% of ceiling. The cell is overwhelmingly overhead-bound: even the minimum ns/p (36.5) implies 68/36.5 = 1.86 GB/s, far below the streaming limit of 68/2.7 ≈ 25 GB/s. There is no regime where the cell transitions to bandwidth-bound; achieved bandwidth never exceeds 10% of ceiling at any measured point. If the hypothesis predicts approaching the streaming ceiling, it falls far short across all N and death rates.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the step function. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions appear (`movi.2d` for zero-initialization), with no `ld1`, no `ldr q` on particle data, and no vector FP. The walk1 computation is offloaded to `bl _halide_b1`; the visible step body is the walk2 render, which operates scalar-wise: `ldp s4, s5` loads single-precision floats, followed by scalar `fadd`, `fmul`, `fcvtzs` for position-to-pixel mapping. The scatter writes RGBA channels via 16 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` with 18 `csel` for 0–255 clamping — four separate byte stores per pixel hit. This byte-granular scatter with branch-heavy bounds checking (`ccmp`, `tbnz`, `b.lo`) explains why bandwidth stays below 10% of ceiling: the render phase cannot stream, and the scalar float pipeline serializes per-particle work.

## Verdict
Refuted — the cell never exceeds 2.53 GB/s (10% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) and sustains only 1.87 GB/s (7.4%) at its best stable large-N point (N=4000000, q=0.25). The step function shows no vectorization (2 `movi.2d` only) and the render scatter's byte-granular `strb`/`ldrb`/`csel` pattern caps bandwidth regardless of death rate or N. The Halide walk1 delegation (`bl _halide_b1`) does not rescue the overall cell from the scalar scatter bottleneck in walk2.
